title: Why Extended Warranties Are Suddenly the Hottest Thing at Car Dealerships - Moto4x
summary: An article explains why dealerships push extended warranties harder than ever, tracing it to profit margins and service-department retention, with tips for negotiating.

assertions.quote: they can earn significantly more on a single extended warranty contract
dealerships are leaning harder on high-margin products to stay profitable

verdicts.note: F&I products have long been a profit center regardless of new-car margins; the causal link to recently shrinking margins is plausible but not independently measured

assertions.quote: they're also ensuring a steady stream of service department revenue for years to come

verdicts.note: Warranty contracts often steer or require service at affiliated shops, plausibly raising dealer service revenue, though the scale of this effect isn't independently quantified

assertions.quote: there's often room for discounts, especially if you're willing to walk away from the deal
Third-party warranty companies often offer similar coverage at lower prices
Many warranties exclude wear items, pre-existing conditions, and damage from neglected maintenance.
Many warranties exclude wear items, pre-existing conditions, and damage from neglected maintenance.
having complete records readily available can mean the difference between approval and denial

verdicts.note: Warranty administrators commonly require proof of maintenance to approve claims, so documentation gaps are a frequent, well-documented cause of denial
